chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abi al-Qasim, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Isḥaq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Kharijah, who said:

A man asked Aba Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a long hadith of his, which he said at its end: 'May I sacrifice my father and mother for you! They narrated from your father regarding the Hajj.' He said: 'Yes, a Hajj and an Umrah,' until he counted ten.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah of Imam al-Husain (peace be upon him) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the exceptional status of visiting Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), equating it to the cumulative reward of ten Hajjs and ten Umrahs. This multiplicity underscores the concept of *thawab* (reward) in Shia tradition, where physical pilgrimage to the Imams serves as a spiritual substitute for and enhancement of the obligatory Hajj to Mecca.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Abil Qāsim, from Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillah (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “May I sacrifice my father and mother for you! It is narrated from your father (a.s.) that (going to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)) is equal to Hajj?!” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes. A Hajj and an ‘Umrah, and another Hajj and ‘Umrah…” Hārūn added that the Imam (a.s.) counted ten Hajj and ten ‘Umrah.
